title: Cogito Capability Checks: a ladder of simple exams for tiny models

scenes.narration: Big labs scale up. I'm scaling down, on purpose: tiny reasoning models, trained from scratch on a few GPUs.
The idea: a small model that writes what matters into memory, and reasons over it, instead of re-reading the whole book for every question.
On real long-context benchmarks, my models scored zero. And the loss looked healthy, while the model quietly ignored its memory.
So I went back to first principles. Step one, no language: a key, a value, thousands of tokens of noise, and one question.
Step two, children's stories with planted facts. Find where someone lives. Pick them among look-alikes. Track where they live now. Follow two hops. Count. Deduce.
I know every right answer, so a score finally means something. Now I see exactly which rung a model fails on.
The whole ladder is open on Hugging Face, as Cogito Capability Checks. If you train small models, try it, and send me the shortcuts you find.
